newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up, hopeful on IMF deal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up, hopeful on IMF deal.

text.p: Pakistani stocks soared on Wednesday amid hopes that the caretaker government will secure delayed tranches from a $600 million IMF standby loan and the index may edge further up on Thursday, dealers said. "The market seems to have overcome its bearish mood and even if there is some selling left there is enough demand to absorb it," dealer Faisal Abbas Bhayani of KAB Securities said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 24.14 points, or 1.63 percent, to end at 1,506.72. Losers led gainers 118 to 101. Turnover fell to 42.84 million shares from 45.17 million on Tuesday.
Muslim Commercial Bank rose 1.25 rupees to 39, Faysal Bank 0.85 to 24.60 and Bank of Punjab 2.0 to 19.75. Dewan Salman Fibre rose 0.65 to 34.55 and Nishat Mills 1.75 to 15.
Hub Power Co rose 0.75 to 34.65 and Pakistan State Oil 2.0 to 390. PTCL rose 0.55 to 32.60. Fauji Fertilizer rose 2.25 to 84.75 and ICI Pakistan 0.65 to 19.40.
